title: hdiutil Deprecation in macOS 27 Golden Gate: Transition to diskutil image
summary: Apple has deprecated the `hdiutil` command-line tool in macOS 27 Golden Gate, replacing it with `diskutil image` for disk image operations. While most functionality is preserved, some options like `-puppetstrings` and `-srcfolder`-related flags are missing. Performance improvements are noted with `diskutil image`, but issues such as lack of verbose logging, permission handling, and the absence of a `-scrub` equivalent remain. The transition may disrupt existing workflows and scripts reliant on `hdiutil`.
key_points: Apple deprecates `hdiutil` in macOS 27 Golden Gate, directing users to `diskutil image` for disk operations.
`diskutil image` supports subcommands like `attach`, `create`, `resize`, `info`, and `chpass`, but lacks some `hdiutil` options (e.g., `-puppetstrings`, `-srcfolder` flags).
`diskutil image` is significantly faster (40-45s vs. 110-115s) and produces smaller disk images compared to `hdiutil`.
`diskutil image` does not trigger authentication prompts for root-owned files, unlike `hdiutil`, leading to failures without manual intervention.
`diskutil image` behaves as if the `-scrub` option is enabled by default, excluding `.Trash/` and temporary files.
Key limitations: poor verbose logging, no built-in permission error handling, and missing `-scrub` option.
Deprecation may break existing scripts and apps (e.g., Knox) that rely on `hdiutil`.
Persistent bug: Both tools still fail to handle `.bnnsir` files (Siri/CoreSpeech data) correctly.
